quest.title: The Toy War: Shots Fired
quest.description: You received a special commission from Leschots Clockwork Workshop. This is a toy shop in the Court of Fontaine. Have they encountered some manner of trouble?
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x40, Enigmatic Copper Mainspring x60, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: This is so annoying.

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: Yes, very annoying.

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: Doesn't this just mean that Lady Furina will sit at the judges' table?

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: Exactly.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Sit at the judges' table"? What does that mean?

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: Oh my, we have guests! Judging from your clothes, you must be outlanders, yes? In that case, it's quite expected that you might not understand our local lingo. Allow me to put it this way: who should sit at the judges' table?

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: The Justices, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: And who is our Chief Justice?

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: Monsieur Neuvillette, naturally.

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: Oh my! Well then, why is our dear Hydro Archon sitting in Monsieur Neuvillette's chair? Come now, tell me, what would the poor people being judged think of that?

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: If it were me, why, I would feel cheated! Our Hydro Archon knows nothing about being a judge!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Well, it does seem like they wouldn't be getting what was advertised...

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: Exactly! Trials will be "not-as-advertised," precisely as you say!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, so it does mean what Paimon thought it did... Wait just a second! Are you sure it's okay for you to make fun of your god like that?

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: Oh, of course! Our Archon loves such jokes.

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: Why, if these words reached her ears, she would tie me to a stone and have me hurled into a deep lake, watching enthusiastically from the sidelines the entire time.

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: But ah, dear guests, do not grieve yet. For our good Arbon is ever so flighty with his words that even a millstone could not sink him.

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: And our Archon would say, "Ah, it's a miracle! Such a romantic ending!" while applauding most loudly. In fact, she might even shed a tear or two.

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: Aye, and she may even bestow upon me a "Model of Romantic Fontaine" medal!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's... not sure what to say here...

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: In any case, let's get to business — might I ask why you have come to our humble store?

response.speaker: Alberre
response.text: Speaking of which, Arbon, don't you think our two guests look like the famous adventurers the boss told us about previously?

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: #Huh, quite so! One with hair like burnished gold, and the other like shining silver... Oh, right! Might the two of you be {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME} and Ms. Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Err, you know us?

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: The boss was asking around at the Adventurers' Guild about adventurers active in Fontaine, and ended up being told about the two of you. Word is that you're a pretty formidable team.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Well, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, looks like we're getting more famous by the day!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph. C'mon, you could show a bit more humility!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well then, what would your boss like from us?

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: Well, unfortunately, he's not in the store right now, so allow us to tell you in his stead.

response.speaker: Alberre
response.text: Just a few words, not to worry.

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: To be brief, our boss would like your help collecting data for his "Champion Duelist Plan."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Champion Duelist Plan"?

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: It is a plan to use champion duelists as the main characters, the development centerpiece, and the focus of our advertising for a new line of clockwork toys. Ah, right, that's our business, by the way — clockwork toys.

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: Also, have the two of you heard of Champion Duelists?

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: Our boss believes this to be an excellent cultural institution of Fontaine — as such, toys of this kind may yet sell very well indeed.

response.speaker: Alberre
response.text: And if they do get popular outside the country, we can also win honor for our nation — two birds with one stone, I say! Ah, I can see Lady Furina herself pinning medals to our chests!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, so that's the situation, huh? But if you're making toy Champion Duelists, what do you need us adventurers for?

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: Well, you can't develop anything without data. And the strength of the Champion Duelists is honed in all manner of perilous places. Getting data on them isn't easy.

response.speaker: Alberre
response.text: But when we heard that the more impressive adventurers do similar things, we thought, why not get adventurers to help us instead...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, Paimon kinda gets it now. You're gonna use adventurers to get the data you need for your line of toy Champion Duelists. Is that it?

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: Well, now, it's not quite that serious. It's more like replacing a Romaritime Flower with a Mallow Tree.

response.speaker: Alberre
response.text: Or, you know, a wooden pillar with a stone one!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Gah. Doesn't all this mean more or less the same thing? That's what you two were talking about from the start, y'know — and we heard it all!

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: Oh, uh, that! We were talking about Lepaute Horlogerie, the watchmaker next-next door. They're way worse than we are, trust me.

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: They call themselves a watchmaker, but they make toys on the sly. Now that's just completely absurd, isn't it?

response.speaker: Alberre
response.text: Indeed. Terribly so!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A watchmaker that sells toys?

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: Exactly! And is that not reprehensible? Come, tell me, what do you like most in this world?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What Paimon likes most? Well, uh, it's her best buddy {NICKNAME}, of course!

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: #In that case, if there was a "{NICKNAME} Puppet Store" somewhere that you traveled from afar to see, only to find that it did not sell {NICKNAME} puppets at all, but instead stocked nothing but a ton of Arbon puppets.

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: Would you not be angered at this betrayal of your expectations? Would you not cry and scream? Would you not send the boss of that store flying with a single punch for denying you the purchase of your dear companion?

response.speaker: Alberre
response.text: Why, I'd be furious! I'd punch the store owner straight into a cell in the Fortress of Meropide. Seriously, who'd buy Arbon puppets anyway?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Well, now that you say so, it would be kinda annoying... What do we do, {NICKNAME}? It would be terrible if puppets of you were to go out of stock!

choices.text: Paimon, it's a red herring. Don't get distracted.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, and they almost got Paimon there, too!

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: Oh, come now, we were just making analogies, and you know what they say — there's no such thing as a perfect analogy. And well, the things we described do happen! After all, you will not find Beryl Conches in Conch Madeleines, will you?

response.speaker: Alberre
response.text: Precisely, and such things will only increase in frequency, until a day comes when watchmakers stop making watches altogether — but we shall not forgive them, oh no, unless they change their name to Lepaute Toymakers!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And there you both go again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You two really love spouting nonsense, don't you? The more you talk, the further off-topic we get! So let's just have it now — what do you need us to do?

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: Well... Actually, we do have one request to make before that. Could you two go to Lepaute Horlogerie next door and do a little investigation there?

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: Watchmaking is their main trade, but their latest toys have become so popular they're stealing our customers. We heard that the store owner gained inspiration for those toys in Mondstadt, and we're curious about what they might be.

response.speaker: Alberre
response.text: For all you know, it might be some alchemy-powered toy that gives off a scent four times as sweet as Sunsettias, which they use to ensnare people. Well, I've heard that there's an alchemist in Mondstadt who can do that, anyway.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A Quadruple-Sweetness Sunsettia? Wouldn't that be...

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: As such, could you please help us check it out, dear guests? Our boss is quite concerned about this matter.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And why won't you go yourselves?

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: Oh, come on now, dear guest, we have reputations to maintain as businesspeople. We can't just walk over there willy-nilly!

response.speaker: Alberre
response.text: Exactly, it's for the sake of our reputation! And is one's reputation not one's all?

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: For my part, I must go tell our boss of your arrival, so please, lend us your aid in this matter.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #To be honest, {NICKNAME}, Paimon's pretty curious. What would toys that take inspiration from Mondstadt look like? Would they really have something to do with alchemy? Let's just go have a look, shall we?

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: Ah, thank you so much! In that case, we shall wait for news from you here!

choices.text: They're selling you a bridge here, you know.
It's no different from "Lady Furina sitting at the judges' table".
Not at all. Could you explain?

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: They are a special institution in Fontaine. If you commit any crime, as you face your trial, you may apply for a duel against a Champion Duelist.

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: Should you prove victorious, you can clear your name and defend your honor, and thus remove the need for a trial. However, defeating a Champion Duelist is no mean feat.

response.speaker: Alberre
response.text: Harder than selling toys, certainly.

choices.text: 'Tis all thanks to you, Ms. Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehehe, haven't you been growing a silver tongue lately? Alrighty then. For that, Paimon shall always share her fortune with you.

choices.text: Is that what Fontainians consider romantic?

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Hello, dear customers. I'm Caron, the owner of this shop. What can I do for you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's a lot of people you've got here. Is there some event going on?

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Oh, no, I wouldn't call it that. We just have a new product. A toy, to be precise — the one at the entrance. If you're interested, you can come and try it out anytime.

talks.objective: Talk to Caron, the shop owner

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Hello, dear customers. I'm Caron, the owner of this shop. What can I do for you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there, boss! We've heard that you've come up with an awesome toy, so we'd like to know more about it.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Haha, of course you can. Still... My elder brother sent you here to seek out information, didn't he?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Your brother? Wait... Actually, how did you know what we were here for?

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Oh, I just saw you walking out from the clockwork workshop, that's all. My brother owns that shop, and I know him, and what he'd do. This is right up his alley.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exposed before we could even get started...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, we should've prepped more before coming over. How were we supposed to know that you're brothers? Ugh, now this isn't just a matter of corporate competition, is it? It's brother against brother!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon, mind your language, please.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sorry boss, Paimon's brain-gears got stuck there for a minute.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Don't worry. Even the best-made toys have components that will get stuck at some point. It's the same with people, you need to take good care of them.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Besides, I don't think you're wrong about how my brother sees our relationship. Regardless, I won't take up more of your time than needed. Let me talk about these toys instead!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Are you sure this is okay? We're... we're supposed to be secretly gathering intel!

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Hahaha, such interesting things you say, dear customers! Our store's real bread and butter is clocks, which we make using techniques handed down from generation to generation.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Toys are just my personal hobby. They bring happiness to people, so if I let more people know about them, is that not the same as spreading happiness?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, that's such a... nice way of thinking about things!

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Haha, my brother would probably say that this line of thinking is too unadventurous... But that aside, why don't you have a look at the toy? I hope you'll like it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I heard that you got your inspiration from Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Indeed, I've liked the place since I was little, and when I went there recently, it was indeed a rewarding experience for me.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: I incorporated the story of an adventurer I met there into the toy, but don't set your expectations too high, alright? In the end, it's just a simple clockwork device.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: An adventurer? So it's not a product of alchemy, then?

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: An alchemical toy? That sounds interesting. But this adventurer made quite the impression. If there's time, I'll tell you his story.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Would you like to try the toy out now? There's nothing quite like experiencing it for yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #We'd love to, but they're still waiting for our reply on the other end. We should get there first, {NICKNAME}, and then come right back! Paimon really wants to try this adventurer toy right away!

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Alright then. Remember, you're always welcome here.

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: Boss, our two guests have returned.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: The two of you are quick indeed... As expected of people recommended by the Adventurers' Guild. I'm Livre, the owner of this shop. Welcome.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there, boss. So you and Caron are brothers! We didn't know about that, and he saw through us right away.

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: Seriously, Alberre? You didn't tell them something this important?

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: Seriously, Arbon? Didn't we agree that you'd tell them? If you're gonna cut anyone's salary, Boss, cut his!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, are you two brothers too?

dialogues.speaker: Arbon & Alberre
dialogues.text: What? Don't call this guy my brother!

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: Ahem... So what you mean to say is that the mission's a bust? You didn't find anything?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, no. Caron is a really nice guy, and he didn't mind even though he knew about us. He even told us that we could try the toy out anytime.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: Hehe, that guy... So, is that toy alchemically-powered?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No, it's an adventurer toy.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: Hmph. Those things are so corny. Didn't he say that he incorporated some adventurers' story into it, or something?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right. How did you know? Did you already investigate the matter, or something?

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: Hah, I just know him all too well. He always puts something sentimental into his toys without caring about the market situation. If you ask me, adventure stories are long out of fashion.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But his shop is very popular, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: That's just ordinary market fluctuations. Once our Champion Duelist lineup takes the stage, we'll have him beat, easy!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But those aren't real Champion Duelists! They're the result of us "out of fashion" adventurers play-acting.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: Hah, what do the two of you know? This is what we call packaging! It's standard practice on the market, and no one cares how exactly you do it.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: We're just going to get the data and put it into some popular toy prototypes, and claim that it's a story about the growth of a Champion Duelist — and that'll do the trick just fine!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? That's it? Paimon feels like there'll definitely be problems this way...

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: It's fine if the story has issues. It's all about the gimmick.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: What would you think if I told you that Arbon and Alberre are in fact ultra-realistic, ultra-high-quality puppets based on the theme of "double act"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? They're puppets? Can puppets look so real!?

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: Of course they can.

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: That's the power of a double act! Tricks can seem very real indeed!

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: See that? That's the power of packaging. Even a gimmick can, when presented the right way, generate interest!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, so it was just a trick! You cheater... You couldn't be more different from your brother.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: Well, that's his problem for not staying in his clockwork lane. If he wants to stick his nose into the toymaking business, it's my duty as his older brother to show him what's what.

choices.text: Quite the dab hand, aren't you?

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: Thanks for the compliments. In that case, eyes up, you two. The data collection will be run by Arbon and Alberre.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, well, we're just gonna turn a blind eye to your brotherly conflict. Just don't skimp on our payments.

choices.text: None more conniving than a merchant, I see.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Hmm... Armand seems to be doing a lot better lately.

dialogues.speaker: Armand
dialogues.text: H—H—Hello, you t—two... My name is... is... A—A—Armand...

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Well, aren't you the customers I saw earlier? Do you need anything?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right, it's us! We've heard that that toy of yours is super awesome so we'd like to know more about it.

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: I need to go tell the boss that the two guests he invited have arrived.

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: Well, go and return quickly, then, before I die of boredom watching the store alone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, there are a ton of people here! Looks like the toys really are popular.
